## Overview

The `centraldogma` package provides a simple workflow that represents the
central dogma of molecular biology. It includes functions for generating a DNA
sequence, transcribing DNA into RNA, splitting RNA into codons, translating
codons into amino acids, and visualizing amino acid frequencies.

## Using the package

First, load the package:

```{r}
library("centraldogma")
```

### Generate a DNA sequence

`generate_dna()` generates a random DNA sequence of a specified length.

```{r}
dna <- generate_dna(30)
dna
```

### Transcribe DNA into RNA

`dna_to_rna()` converts a DNA sequence into RNA by replacing thymine (T)
with uracil (U).

```{r}
rna <- dna_to_rna(dna)
rna
```

### Split RNA into codons

`split_into_codons()` divides the RNA sequence into groups of three
nucleotides.

```{r}
codons <- split_into_codons(rna)
codons
```

### Translate codons into amino acids

Function 4 translates the RNA codons into their corresponding amino acids
using the codon table included in the package.
